+    "math_and_domain": "The Poincare squared-distance expression is dimensionally well-typed for projected vectors in the stated ball, with c=1 and positive denominators because ||x||,||y||<=R<1/sqrt(c). Exp_0 and the Euclidean residual subtraction operate on 32-dimensional vectors consistently. The stated c->0 squared-distance limit 4||x-y||^2 is correct for fixed projected x,y; the flat arm uses this limit, retains the same fixed projection ball, and does not apply the undefined curvature-dependent radius at c=0. The clamp and stable arcosh expression are specified. No undefined scored-distance domain or missing flat limit is apparent.",
+    "control": "The declared flat arm is the same implementation and capacity, with architecture, parameters, initialization, transition targets, losses, training-only inputs, projection ball, optimizer, schedule, seeds and budget held fixed; only c/distance varies. No separately designed or higher-capacity control is proposed.",
+    "leakage_and_protocol": "The stated fitting inputs and static transition targets are training-only. SID assignment is global per item and excludes user, history, request and batch context. Validation and test are restricted to diagnostics and the registered downstream evaluation, not fitting or model selection. The frozen protocol specifies the existing Stage2 encoder/optimizer/schedule/batch/seeds/initialization, 3000 epochs, three levels of 256 codes, latent dimension 32, and no sweep or early stopping. No future-event or prediction-time user-context leakage is specified.",
+    "stage2_leading_indicators": "The registered Stage2 leading indicators include validation Hard-L1 ER on the exact frozen 52855 validation pairs, distinct two-token prefixes, and L3 statistics (collision and refinement gain), alongside valid L1 positive hit rate and conditional G3. Each has a direction, minimum effect, and paired-seed arithmetic-mean aggregation rule. These are diagnostics rather than a claim that Stage2 proves behavioral gain.",
+    "falsifier_and_nulls": "The manifest gives mechanically checkable passed, mixed and falsified conditions in terms of each registered effect meeting its stated direction and minimum effect; mixed denotes both a met and a missed effect, while falsified denotes a miss without a met effect. Any NULL comparison is explicitly inconclusive and is not imputed or replaced."
+  }
+}
*** End Patch
